# Releasing Pit

Pit is distributed only through GitHub: `main` for the latest changes and tags for pinned releases. Keep `private: true` in `package.json`; do not publish Pit to npm.

## Prepare

1. Confirm the release tracking issue is current.
2. Confirm the intended Pi version has been tested and documented without overstating compatibility.
3. Review dependency updates and run `npm audit`.
4. Update `CHANGELOG.md`, `package.json`, and `package-lock.json` to the release version, and point the README's pinned install example at the new tag. After users update, Pi shows them the changelog entries under each `## [X.Y.Z]` heading newer than the version they last saw, so write entries for Pit's users and keep the heading format; `npm run package:check` requires a heading for the `package.json` version.
5. Keep the README's primary install command unpinned (`pi install git:github.com/cv/pit`); `npm run package:check` enforces both.
6. Run a full-history secret scan before the first public release or after adding substantial generated/session artifacts.
7. Review the dry-run package file list and size.

## Validate

```sh
npm run check
npm test
npm run coverage
npm run package:check
npm run quality:audit
npm pack --dry-run
```

Review the final diff and confirm a clean worktree. Changes to TUI, extension loading, saved functions, sandboxing, progress, or rendering require an interactive reload smoke test before the tracking issue is closed.

## Publish

1. Commit the version and release documentation on a `release-X.Y.Z` branch, without a closing keyword, and open a pull request. `main` is protected: it requires a pull request and up-to-date checks, including for administrators.
2. After its checks pass, rebase-merge the pull request and verify CI for the resulting `main` commit.
3. Create and push an annotated tag on that merged `main` commit:

   ```sh
   git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "pit vX.Y.Z"
   git push origin vX.Y.Z
   ```

4. The Release workflow validates the package and tag, then publishes a release with generated notes and no assets: Pit installs from the tagged source. GitHub can deliver one tag push more than once; runs for a tag wait for each other, and a later run leaves a release already published at the tagged commit unchanged.
5. Verify the release targets the tagged commit and has no assets. Then, before declaring delivery complete, install the tag's runtime dependencies from a fresh clone and run the sandbox:

   ```sh
   git clone --depth 1 --branch vX.Y.Z https://github.com/cv/pit.git /tmp/pit-vX.Y.Z
   cd /tmp/pit-vX.Y.Z
   npm ci --omit=dev
   node -e "import('@earendil-works/pi-codemode').then(async ({ CodemodeSandbox }) => console.log(await new CodemodeSandbox().execute('return 1 + 1')))"
   ```

In Pit, `release.verifyPublished({ tag: "vX.Y.Z" })` performs step 5 and reports every problem it finds.

## Install and smoke-test the tag

Install the exact tag into a throwaway agent directory so the check does not change your own configuration. Call the Pi binary you intend to test by path: an older `pi` earlier on `PATH` may not support `install` and instead starts a session.

```sh
HOME=/tmp/pit-smoke/home PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=/tmp/pit-smoke/agent \
  /path/to/pi install git:github.com/cv/pit@vX.Y.Z < /dev/null
```

The installed package is under `/tmp/pit-smoke/agent/git/github.com/cv/pit`. Pass that directory as `cwd` to `ux.manageSession` to exercise the installed tag in an isolated Pi, or install it in your own Pi with `pi install git:github.com/cv/pit@vX.Y.Z`.

Run `/reload` after installing or updating the tag, then test:

- a one-shot TypeScript call;
- hashed read and edit behavior;
- shell success, failure, cancellation, and timeout;
- expanded partial and final TUI rendering;
- session, project, and user saved-function behavior, plus read-only global inspection;
- model refresh and selection;
- package update from the exact tag.

Correct release-blocking defects in a patch release rather than moving an existing tag.
# Changelog

Notable changes to Pit are documented here. GitHub release notes remain the authoritative detailed record for each tagged release.

## [Unreleased]

## [0.35.0] - 2026-11-11

### Added

- `session.*` on pi-durable hosts: `outline`, `inspectEntry`, `elide`, and `summarize` rewrite the conversation's context with pi-durable edits, and `setNote`/`notes` keep notes in a conversation document shown as the `pit_notes` section, which pi-durable re-sends after compaction and forks inherit. As on Pi, a change applies only if its call succeeds, after the current tool round with `when: "now"` and notes, and by default when the run answers, through an `afterRun` hook. See [Context editing and notes](docs/durable.md#context-editing-and-notes).
- `pit/durable` exports Pit's `typescript` tool for hosts built on `@earendil-works/pi-durable`, such as pi-action. `createPitDurableExtension({ cwd, agentDir, trustProject, ui, log })`, also exported as `createPiDurableExtension` and listed under `pi.durable` in `package.json`, returns an extension with the tool and prompt sections for its guidelines and the user and project function catalogs. Session functions are conversation entries, so a reopened Harness and forks keep them; nested `tools.*` calls go through the host's `executeTool()` and reach every other callable tool, including pi-durable's coding tools, and questions (`ui.*` and the confirmations `functions.*` asks for) work on asynchronous hosts: Pit answers them from a `ui.answer` entry in the conversation or posts them through the host's `ui.ask` and ends the turn, so nothing waits for a person. Interactive hosts can still pass blocking dialogs, during which the program deadline pauses. Project trust is off by default, project function promotion and removal ask through the host's dialogs (and fail without them), and `session.*`, `commands.*`, `models.set`, model requests, and `workspace.viewImage` report that they are unavailable. The entry loads without Pi's coding agent, Pi's TUI, or TypeBox, and `@earendil-works/pi-durable` is an optional peer dependency. See [Pit on pi-durable hosts](docs/durable.md).

## [0.34.0] - 2026-11-09

### Changed

- `/pit-reflect` reviews the work since its previous run in the session unless given a focus. It asks once before promoting tested helpers to the project or user scope instead of leaving them session-scoped, finishes its changes in the same turn, and ends with next steps you can approve: files to commit with a suggested message, pending promotions, and required reloads or smoke tests.
- Pit depends on `oxfmt` 0.75.0.

## [0.33.0] - 2026-11-02

### Added

- Pi shows Pit's changelog after an update: entries newer than the version you last ran appear under "Extension Updates" on the next fresh launch. `npm run package:check` requires a `## [X.Y.Z]` heading for the `package.json` version, the heading Pi matches.
- `models.classify` and `models.generateImages` report `usage.costBilled`: true when `usage.cost` is what the provider billed, false when Pi estimated it from catalog prices.
- Collapsed rows name the key you configured for expanding tool rows: a long model note ends with `… 4 more lines (ctrl+o to expand)`, and a result with more than three images with `… 2 more images; ctrl+o to list`. An unbound key keeps the previous text.

### Changed

- **Breaking:** Pit supports Pi 1.5.0, the version `package-lock.json` now pins: `@earendil-works/pi-codemode` 1.5.0, which Pit installs as its own copy, and, for development, tests, and the `peerDependencies` ranges, `pi-coding-agent` and `pi-tui` 1.5.0. `typebox` stays 1.3.27, the version Pi 1.5.0 loads.
- An expanded `typescript` row highlights its source once and reuses it while the source and the theme's syntax colors stay the same, instead of on every spinner tick and progress update.

### Fixed

- A command run without progress output that Pi stops because its output exceeded Pi's capture limit, new in Pi 1.5.0, is no longer reported as a timeout: its `stderr` explains the limit when the command wrote none, `truncated` is true, and with `raise: true` it throws an ordinary `Error`, not a `TimeoutError`.

## [0.32.0] - 2026-10-26

### Added

- User-wide `allowedTools` defaults in `$PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/pit.json` (`~/.pi/agent/pit.json`), which apply in untrusted projects too. A trusted project's `allowedTools` replaces them; omit the key to inherit or use `[]` to clear. An invalid or unreadable project file grants no exceptions rather than inheriting. `paths` stays project-only and is ignored, with a warning, in the user file. Configuration warnings name the file's full path, and an unreadable `pit.json` is reported as a warning instead of failing session start.

### Changed

- `npm run package:check` requires every package Pit shares with the pinned Pi to be the exact version Pi requires in `package-lock.json`: today `@earendil-works/pi-codemode` 1.4.0, `pi-tui` 1.4.0, and `typebox` 1.3.27. Dependabot no longer proposes `typebox` updates, which move only with a Pi upgrade; [#335](https://github.com/cv/pit/pull/335) had proposed `typebox` 1.4.2 for development while Pi 1.4.0 loads 1.3.27. Development uses `oxlint` 1.89.0.

## [0.31.0] - 2026-10-23

### Changed

- **Breaking:** Pit supports Pi 1.4.0, the version `package-lock.json` now pins: `@earendil-works/pi-codemode` 1.4.0, which Pit installs as its own copy, and, for development, tests, and the `peerDependencies` ranges, `pi-coding-agent` and `pi-tui` 1.4.0. `typebox` stays 1.3.27, the version Pi 1.4.0 loads. Pi 1.4.0's limit of two concurrent codemode workers applies to Pi's own codemode tool, not to Pit's sandbox, so `typescript` calls do not queue behind it or count toward `PI_CODEMODE_MAX_WORKERS`.
- `session.summarize` keeps its summary limit, 0.8 × the compaction `reserveTokens` capped at the model's output limit, as Pit's own: Pi 1.4.0 no longer applies it to compaction summaries, because their generation budget also covers reasoning, while Pit's limit counts only the summary text. Its error now states the formula instead of calling it Pi's compaction-summary budget.

## [0.30.1] - 2026-10-20

### Fixed

- When top-level `params` can't be passed to a program, validation says so instead of reporting TypeScript's raw arity error on the generated `program({} as PitDependencies, params)` call, which the program never wrote. A program without an input parameter gets the fix (declare one after the dependencies, or omit `params`); other mismatches keep TypeScript's detail under a `params` heading. Errors in the program's own code keep their location and excerpt ([#328](https://github.com/cv/pit/pull/328)).
- Empty `params` (`{}` or `[]`), which some models send on every call, no longer fail a program that declares no input parameter; the program runs as if `params` were omitted. Non-empty `params` still fail there, and empty `params` are still checked against a declared input type ([#329](https://github.com/cv/pit/pull/329)).

name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"

permissions:
  contents: write

# GitHub can deliver one tag push more than once. Runs for a tag wait for each other, so a later
# run sees the release an earlier one published.
concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    name: release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - name: Use lockfile-compatible npm
        run: npm install --global npm@12.2.0
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci
      - name: Verify tag and package version
        run: |
          package_version=$(node --input-type=module -e 'import manifest from "./package.json" with { type: "json" }; process.stdout.write(manifest.version)')
          test "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" = "v$package_version"
      - name: Audit runtime dependencies
        run: npm audit --omit=dev
      - name: Verify package
        run: npm run package:check
      - name: Run static checks
        run: npm run check
      # The tagged commit passed tests and coverage in CI; Pit installs from the tagged source.
      - name: Inspect package contents
        run: npm pack --dry-run
      - name: Create GitHub release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
